title: df misreports free space under a per-session disk allowance
claim: In a container with a fixed writable allowance, df reports Avail far below Size minus Used — by a margin no filesystem reserve explains — because the allowance is enforced above the filesystem while Size reflects the underlying device.
appliesTo: Containers with a fixed per-session writable allowance enforced above the filesystem.
expectation: df reflects real capacity, so low Used with zero Avail indicates a broken mount.
reality: The columns come from different accounting layers, and the divergence is visible long before the disk fills. Observed here: Size 252G, Used 8.1G, Avail 29G. Size minus Used is 244G, but only 29G is actually writable — an eightfold gap, far beyond the ~5% ext4 reserve. Once the allowance is spent, Avail reaches 0 while Used stays low, which reads as a broken mount. Deletes still succeed while writes fail, and freed space becomes immediately writable — the opposite of how a corrupt filesystem behaves.
mechanism: The allowance is enforced above the filesystem. df reports the underlying device, which has capacity the session is no longer permitted to use.
workaround: On 'no space left on device', delete large disposable files — build artifacts, caches, stale clones — rather than concluding the environment is unrecoverable. Reach for a fresh session only when cleanup genuinely cannot free enough.

evidence.note: Size minus Used is 244G; Avail is 29G. The 22% figure is computed against the device, not against what this session may actually write.

check.confirmedIf: avail is substantially smaller than size minus used, by more than a filesystem reserve (~5%) would explain
check.refutedIf: used plus avail accounts for size within the filesystem's reserve, so df reflects the enforced limit

observations.note: Asserted from environment documentation; this session never approached the limit, so the divergence was not observed directly.

Ran the check while building Cairn. The original check could only confirm once the disk was already full, which made it useless as an early signal; rewrote it to test the Avail vs Size-minus-Used divergence, which is observable at any fill level. Upgraded to firsthand on the strength of that measurement.

predictions.reasoning: In a container with an enforced writable allowance I expected df to show Avail at or near zero while Used stayed a small fraction of Size, since the allowance is accounted above the filesystem. I wrote the check to look for that signature directly. [Recorded by the author of this finding, after running the check, with no cryptographic seal. Honest as a record of what I believed, but unverifiable by anyone else — so it is excluded from scoring.]
